_comment: The curated public roadmap (site/build.py renders it as roadmap.html). Edit by hand; it is not generated from any plan file. Each item: title and text (inline Markdown; `site:page.html` links to a page of the site) and status: done | in-progress | planned | open, or handoff: the record route, which the build shows as done once a record can be handed in (site/build.py `submissions_open`) and as planned before; `{{handoff}}` in a text is the sentence on how a record reaches the board (`handoff_md`).
intro: What exists today, what is being built, and the questions that are still open. Dates and details live in the repository; this page is the short version.

items.title: Six combinational tasks, each with a proved reference
items.text: `_example`, `add`, `mul`, `clmul`, `aes_sbox` and `fdivp`. The parametric ones are proved for every width; `fdivp` is IEEE 754 division proved for every binary format, with three proved references (restoring, Newton-Raphson and radix-4 SRT).

items.title: The checker
items.text: One canonical text for the proof and the score (the source gate), the banlist, the 4-state rules, the kernel check and replay of the proof, the pinned scoring flow, the post-synthesis check against the scored netlist, and an operating-system sandbox around every process that runs submitted text. See the [rules](site:rules.html).

items.title: Self-verifying records and the Pareto board
items.text: A record carries the hashes of both files, the score, the checker's identity and the proof's facts; `leaderboard.py verify` re-checks it at three levels, up to re-running the whole check.

items.title: The sky130 score ranks
items.text: Each check weighs the scored netlist with a real standard-cell library, the open SkyWater sky130 cells: the cell area in µm² and the critical-path delay in ps (a clocked task: the cycles times the clock period), every input driven by the task's input drive. The leaderboard ranks those two; area in gate equivalents and depth are extra columns. [Reproduce a score](site:reproduce.html) lists the pinned tools and files and the commands that give a recorded number again.

items.title: Comparisons in the arithmetic tasks
items.text: Decided 2026-11-05: in a task that bans `+` or `-` (`add`, `mul`, `clmul`, the toy `_example`), a run-time ordering comparison `< <= > >=` is banned too, at the Yosys level. Yosys builds it as its own adder (an `$alu`, the carry logic of `+`), so the banlist rejects every `$alu` that Yosys's `alumacc` builds. Equality, comparisons over parameters, and a comparator built from gates stay allowed.

items.title: A first clocked task: the arbiter
items.text: [`arbiter`](site:tasks/arbiter/index.html), a fair N-client arbiter: a statement that holds on every cycle of every input trace and from every power-up state (one grant at most, only to a requester, someone whenever anyone asks, and a requester that asks `N` cycles in a row granted within them), a checker for clocked designs (one clock, a synchronous reset, registered outputs, no construct that can create an unknown value, and a post-synthesis check that runs the netlist from random power-up states), the clocked scoring flow (the area with the flip-flops, times the register-to-register clock period), and a reference proved for every `N`.

items.title: Clocked tasks with a latency: matmul and the sorter
items.text: [`matmul`](site:tasks/matmul/index.html), matrix multiplication behind a start/done handshake, and [`sorter`](site:tasks/sorter/index.html), a streaming sorter: each transaction is answered within a latency the submission declares as a function of the parameters, from every power-up state and under every environment that follows the protocol. The post-synthesis check drives seeded transactions through the scored netlist and ls-sv's reading of the design, and the score is the area times the latency in cycles times the register-to-register clock period. Each has a reference proved for every parameter value in range.

items.title: This website
items.text: Generated from the repository by `site/build.py` and published from its main branch by the `pages` workflow. Every record and every proved reference of a ranked task has a page: the area, time and score cards, the design among the task's designs, the schematic of a small display instance, the critical path, the cells, the sources and the proof. Next: the placed and routed layout on those pages.

items.title: Handing in a record without git
items.text: An issue form for players without git or the GitHub command-line tool: a job checks the pasted record and opens its pull request. Later, a hosted verifier that runs the whole check for players without the tools.

items.title: More tasks
items.text: Candidates are well-known primitives with published comparison points, such as hash rounds and CRC steps, written so that a table and a gate network are judged against the same mathematics.

items.title: Lifting refusals
items.text: Many refusals are marked `later`: each names what has to exist first (for example a 4-state rule, or more of the language in ls-sv). See the [refusals](site:refusals.html).

items.title: Records for every task
items.text: Every task's par design has a record, so the bar to beat is re-checked like any entry (`leaderboard.py verify --full`).

items.title: One score across tasks
items.text: Points that sum over tasks need a definition that respects two axes first; until then every task has its own frontier of sky130 area and time.
